# Aim and data

This report demonstrates a reproducible workflow for exploratory human brain DNA methylation array analysis in an Alzheimer's disease context. It is a methods demonstration, not a claim of biological discovery.

The data are from GEO accession GSE212682 and were generated with an Illumina MethylationEPIC array. All eligible middle frontal gyrus samples with diagnosis codes 0 (control) and 2 (AD) entered sample QC. The intermediate diagnosis group was excluded. The table shows the samples that passed QC and entered the primary model.

```{r sample-summary}
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(metadata$diagnosis)),
             col.names = c("Diagnosis", "Samples"))
```

GEO reports age as `90+` for this cohort. The analysis retains that value and excludes age from the models. Cell proportions are EpiSCORE estimates published by the original study.

```{r metadata-summary}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  variable = c("region", "diagnosis", "sex", "batch", "bisulfite_batch", "age_raw"),
  observed_values = c(
    paste(unique(metadata$region), collapse = "; "),
    paste(unique(metadata$diagnosis), collapse = "; "),
    paste(unique(metadata$sex), collapse = "; "),
    paste(unique(metadata$batch), collapse = "; "),
    paste(unique(metadata$bisulfite_batch), collapse = "; "),
    paste(unique(metadata$age_raw), collapse = "; ")
  )
))
cell_proportions <- metadata[startsWith(names(metadata), "proportion_")]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  cell_type = sub("^proportion_", "", names(cell_proportions)),
  minimum = vapply(cell_proportions, min, numeric(1)),
  median = vapply(cell_proportions, median, numeric(1)),
  maximum = vapply(cell_proportions, max, numeric(1))
), digits = 3)
```

# QC and normalization

Samples with a mean detection p-value above 0.01 or a missing or non-finite mean were excluded before normalization. The QC table covers every eligible sample.

```{r qc-summary}
knitr::kable(qc)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  samples = nrow(qc),
  samples_failed = sum(qc$qc_status == "fail"),
  sex_mismatches = sum(sex$sex_mismatch, na.rm = TRUE)
))
```

![Sample detection p-values](../results/qc_mean_detection_p.pdf)

![Intensity QC](../results/qc_intensity.pdf)

Sex prediction was compared with the supplied metadata. A mismatch is a flag for investigation, not proof that either field is correct.

```{r sex-summary}
knitr::kable(sex)
```

Noob normalization was used to correct background signal and dye-related technical differences. The raw-versus-Noob beta density comparison was generated from the normalized objects.

![Raw versus Noob beta distributions](../results/normalisation_beta_density.pdf)

# Probe filtering and missingness

The filter removes sex-chromosome probes, probes with annotated CpG or single-base-extension SNPs, and the IDs flagged by the Zhou EPIC v1 hg19 `MASK_general` annotation from release `20180909`. The mask addresses mapping ambiguity and other documented probe issues. See the annotation provenance in `data/reference/README.md`.

```{r filtering}
knitr::kable(filters)
```

The final beta matrix contained complete values, so the workflow used the observed values directly. The mask removed `r mask_summary$probes_excluded` probes that passed the preceding filters. The same primary model was fit with and without the mask using the same normalized assays and covariates to assess its effect on probe rankings.

```{r mask-comparison}
knitr::kable(mask_summary)
knitr::kable(head(mask_comparison, 10))
```

# PCA and batch assessment

PCA describes variation before adjustment. The array-batch and bisulfite-batch labels identify the same groups in this cohort. The primary model includes array batch as a fixed effect. Batches containing only one diagnosis contribute to nuisance estimates and residual variation. The direct within-batch diagnosis contrast comes from batches that include both groups.

```{r batch-overlap}
knitr::kable(batch_overlap)
```

![PCA by diagnosis](../results/pca_by_diagnosis.pdf)

![PCA by batch](../results/pca_by_batch.pdf)

```{r pca-tables}
pca_variance <- read.delim(file.path(results_dir, "pca_variance.tsv"), check.names = FALSE)
pc_tests <- read.delim(file.path(results_dir, "pc_variable_associations.tsv"), check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(head(pca_variance, 5))
knitr::kable(pc_tests)
```

# Differential methylation

The primary model fits the AD versus control contrast on M-values with limma and adjusts for array batch, recorded sex, and estimated neuronal proportion. Using neuronal proportion as a single covariate preserves degrees of freedom in the smaller shared-batch fit. Adjusted delta beta is the coefficient from the same design fitted on the beta scale. The workflow verifies full column rank and positive residual degrees of freedom before either fit. The displayed probes are ranked by the primary limma p-value.

```{r differential}
knitr::kable(model_design)
knitr::kable(diff_summary)
differential <- read.delim(file.path(results_dir, "differential_top.tsv"), check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(head(differential, 10))
```

![Differential methylation volcano plot](../results/differential_volcano.pdf)

![Differential methylation QQ plot](../results/differential_qq.pdf)

The primary genomic inflation factor is `r sprintf("%.3f", diff_summary$genomic_inflation_factor)`. The QQ plot and inflation factor describe departures from the expected null p-value distribution.

# Shared-batch sensitivity analysis

The sensitivity fit uses only array batches with both diagnosis groups. It uses the same covariates and the same filtered probes so the estimates can be compared probe by probe. Both models share samples. Their agreement measures describe sensitivity to the cohort restriction, and the smaller fit has fewer residual degrees of freedom.

The M-value effect correlation is `r sprintf("%.3f", sensitivity$m_effect_pearson_r)`. Among the 100 primary top-ranked probes, `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * sensitivity$top_m_direction_agreement)` have the same effect direction. The primary and shared-batch fits had `r sensitivity$primary_passing_both_cutoffs` and `r sensitivity$shared_passing_both_cutoffs` probes, respectively, meeting both FDR < 0.05 and absolute adjusted delta beta ≥ 0.05.

```{r sensitivity}
knitr::kable(sensitivity, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(head(sensitivity_top, 10), digits = 4)
```

# DMRcate

DMRcate uses the primary covariate design and EPICv1 annotation. Region calling uses FDR-based smoothing over a 1000 bp window and requires a minimum of two CpGs.

```{r dmr}
knitr::kable(dmr_summary)
dmr_ranges <- read.delim(file.path(results_dir, "dmr_ranges.tsv"), check.names = FALSE)
if (nrow(dmr_ranges)) knitr::kable(head(dmr_ranges, 10))
```

# Enrichment

`missMethyl::gometh` accounts for the unequal number of array probes mapping to genes. It uses the 100 CpGs with lowest primary limma p-values and all filtered CpGs as the background. The results describe exploratory enrichment of that ranked list.

```{r enrichment}
knitr::kable(enrichment_summary)
knitr::kable(head(enrichment[, c("collection", "pathway_id", "Description", "P.DE", "FDR")], 10))
```

![Top exploratory pathways](../results/enrichment_top_pathways.pdf)

# Limitations

- The cohort covers one brain region, with diagnosis overlap in only part of the batch structure.
- Age is supplied as `90+` and has no usable numeric variation here.
- Bulk brain tissue estimates adjust for neuronal proportion, which leaves possible confounding by other cell types and uncertainty in the published estimates.
- The independent frontal-cortex comparison is documented separately in `docs/replication.md` because it uses another platform and cohort design.
- Elevated genomic inflation warrants caution when interpreting the p-values. The shared-batch comparison uses overlapping samples.
- The full differential table is kept locally because it exceeds GitHub's file-size limit.
